{{multiple image

In [[geometry]], a '''polygon with holes''' is an area-connected planar [[polygon]] with one external boundary and one or more interior boundaries (holes).<ref>{{citation
 | last = Somerville | first = D. M. Y. | author-link = Duncan Sommerville
 | contribution = IX.4: Polyhedra with ring-shaped faces
 | contribution-url = https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.220891/page/n165
 | pages = 144–145
 | publisher = Methuen & Co.
 | title = An Introduction To The Geometry Of <math>N</math> Dimensions
 | year = 1929}}</ref> Polygons with holes can be [[dissection (geometry)|dissected]] into multiple polygons by adding new edges, so they are not frequently needed.

An ordinary polygon can be called [[simply-connected]], while a polygon-with-holes is ''multiply-connected''. An ''H''-holed-polygon is ''H''-''connected''.<ref>{{citation
 | last = O'Rourke | first = Joseph | author-link = Joseph O'Rourke (professor)
 | contribution = Chapter 5: Holes
 | contribution-url = https://www.science.smith.edu/~jorourke/books/ArtGalleryTheorems/Art_Gallery_Chapter_5.pdf
 | isbn = 0-19-503965-3
 | pages = 125–145
 | publisher = Oxford University Press
 | series = International Series of Monographs on Computer Science
 | title = Art Gallery Theorems and Algorithms
 | volume = 3
 | year = 1987}}</ref>

== Degenerate holes==
[[Degeneracy (mathematics)|Degenerate]] cases may be considered, but a well-formed holed-polygon must have no contact between exterior and interior boundaries, or between interior boundaries. Nondegenerate holes should have 3 or more sides, excluding internal point boundaries ([[monogon]]s) and single edge boundaries ([[digon]]s).

== Boundary orientation==
[[Computational geometry]] algorithms which process polygons with holes, such as in order to draw their interiors or to perform a [[Point_in_polygon|point in polygon test]], may require that the exterior boundary is distinguished from the interior boundaries by their [[Curve orientation|orientation]], the order in which the points are listed;<ref>{{citation
 | last = Urrutia | first = Jorge | author-link = Jorge Urrutia Galicia
 | contribution = Art Gallery and Illumination Problems
 | doi = 10.1016/b978-044482537-7/50023-1
 | isbn = 9780444825377
 | pages = 973–1027
 | publisher = Elsevier
 | title = Handbook of Computational Geometry
 | year = 2000}}</ref> commonly, the exterior boundary is listed in counter-clockwise order, and interior boundaries in clockwise order. This allows the interior area to be defined as ''left'' of each edge, regardless of whether that edge is part of an exterior or interior boundary.

== Conversion to ordinary polygon==
A ''polygon with holes'' can be transformed into an ordinary unicursal boundary path by adding (degenerate) connecting double-edges between boundaries, or by [[dissection (geometry)|dissecting]] or [[Triangulation (geometry)|triangulating]] it into 2 or more simple polygons.
:[[File:Holed-polygon-dissections.png|320px|thumb|left|Example conversion of a single-holed polygon by connecting edges, or [[dissection (geometry)|dissection]]]]
{{clear|left}}

== In polyhedra==

''Polygons with holes'' can be seen as [[face (geometry)|faces]] in [[polyhedra]], like a [[cube]] with a smaller cube externally placed on one of its [[square]] [[Face (geometry)|faces]] (augmented), with their common surfaces removed. A [[toroidal polyhedron]] can also be defined connecting a holed-face to a holed-faced on the opposite side (excavated). The [[1-skeleton]] (vertices and edges) of a polyhedron with holed-faces is not a connected graph. Each set of connected edges will make a separate polyhedron if their edge-connected holes are replaced with faces.

The [[Euler characteristic]] of hole-faced polyhedron is χ = ''V'' − ''E'' + ''F'' = 2(1−''g'') + ''H'', [[Genus (mathematics)|genus]] ''g'', for ''V'' vertices, ''E'' edges, ''F'' faces, and ''H'' holes in the faces.

;Examples with degenerate holes
A face with a point hole is considered a [[monogon]]al hole, adding one vertex, and one edge, and can attached to a degenerate [[monogonal hosohedron]] hole, like a [[Cylinder#Right circular cylinders|cylinder]] hole with zero radius. A face with a degenerate [[digon]] hole adds 2 vertices and 2 coinciding edges, where the two edges attach to two coplanar faces, as a [[dihedron]] hole.
